claims.claim: The arrival read-aloud describes the village through its housing stock and street pattern rather than through its inhabitants.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: mostly made up of steep-roofed cottages, separated by twisting streets

claims.claim: The column then lists the settlement's important locations by name and numbers them as labelled sub-entries.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: The following areas in Icehaven are important to this encounter

claims.claim: A second official column names a governing officer as an invented office title plus given name plus surname, followed by the plain English office in apposition.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Taskhand Durth Mirimm, the current governor
claims.page: 'The Wastes of Xhorhas and the City of Jigow'

claims.claim: The same column qualifies its own size label, calling Jigow a small city by population while describing its extent as a sprawl of towns.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Jigow is a small city by population, but its sprawl of towns
claims.page: 'The Wastes of Xhorhas and the City of Jigow'

claims.claim: The same column ties each read-aloud to the precise moment and threshold at which it is spoken.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Battle of the Braggarts', 2020
claims.quote: Read or paraphrase the following as the characters enter the Wartpimple Tavern

claims.claim: An official D&D Beyond column advises compressing an unremarkable stretch into a single sentence rather than accumulating uninspired description.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Trek to Ten-Towns', 2020
claims.quote: better to simply describe the day’s travel in a single sentence

claims.claim: The same column tells the DM to vary the wording of a repeated transition so the read-aloud does not sound scripted.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Trek to Ten-Towns', 2020
claims.quote: so it doesn't seem like you're reading from a script

claims.claim: A reporter covering the publisher's own preview says the 2024 settlement generator's first roll produces the town's defining feature, giving a Sprawling Cemetery in the demonstration.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: the town's defining feature is [roll the dice] a Sprawling Cemetery

claims.claim: The same report gives the current-calamity roll's demonstration result as monsters infesting the settlement.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: What current calamity is befalling the town: Monsters infest the settlement

claims.claim: The same report shows the leadership roll returning a political condition rather than a person, an illegitimate leader causing civil unrest.
claims.source: Randy, Gaming Nexus, reporting a Wizards of the Coast preview with Chris Perkins, 10 Oct 2024
claims.quote: Local leaders: An illegitimate leader causing civil unrest

claims.claim: The freely licensed System Reference Document 5.2.1 contains no settlement-description rules: its four occurrences of settlement are all inside spell and equipment text.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, System Reference Document 5.2.1 (CC-BY-4.0), 2025
claims.page: whole document; grep over extracted text

claims.claim: Neither freely licensed SRD, 5.1 nor 5.2.1, mentions read-aloud or boxed text anywhere, so no lawful open-licence source carries the form.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, System Reference Document 5.1 (2016) and 5.2.1 (2025)
claims.page: whole documents; grep over extracted text

claims.claim: An official D&D Beyond article reprints the published Phandalin arrival passage and calls it boxed text.
claims.source: Mike Bernier, 'Visit Phandalin, D&D's Most Popular Starter Town!', D&D Beyond, 18 Sep 2023
claims.quote: The boxed text above serves as a fantastic base

claims.claim: The published Phandalin boxed text sizes the town by counting its buildings rather than its people.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Dragon of Icespire Peak boxed text, reprinted in D&D Beyond's Phandalin article
claims.quote: which consists of forty or fifty simple log buildings
claims.page: 'Tips For Running Phandalin in Your Games', quoted boxed text, sourced to Dragon of Icespire Peak

claims.claim: The same published passage states the town's defences as two absences rather than as a description.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Dragon of Icespire Peak boxed text, reprinted in D&D Beyond's Phandalin article
claims.quote: The town has no walls and no garrison
claims.page: 'Tips For Running Phandalin in Your Games', quoted boxed text
